turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leo Bennett, twenty-four. Sit down. What's the problem?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, so my heart keeps doing this fluttery racing thing, mostly at night, and I get really puffed going up the stairs to the flat. My partner's been on at me for ages to come in but I kept putting it...
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long for the fluttering?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, three weeks. No, wait, nearer six weeks. It kicked off when I was doing those all-nighters for the accountancy exams.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless for six weeks as well?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, six weeks for both, about four nights a week. Both the fluttering and the breathlessness are worse at night lying down, on the stairs, and before an exam or the Monday meetings. I don't think it's stress though, I'm not a stressed person, everyone...
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain with it?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I drink loads of coffee. Four mugs... actually it's six, easy, and the energy drinks on top. Monster, the green ones, my mate at the cinema swears by them for late shifts and...
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain. Yes or no?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain in the chest.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blackouts? Nearly fainting?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I did feel a bit swimmy once in the queue at Pret, but that was just because I hadn't eaten, totally separate, and the sandwich was...
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizziness with the palpitations themselves?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, yeah, light-headed when it starts. I couldn't tell you when that bit began, exactly. If I sit up it eases off. Not spinning, just floaty.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sweating?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really, no.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it wake you? How many hours are you sleeping?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh the cinema roster's just changed and I'm on lates, which is grim, the last bus is a nightmare and...
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. Four hours, sometimes five, then I'm awake with the heart going.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every night, or only some?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every night. Maybe four nights a week, and pretty much always before a meeting.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many energy drinks a day?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Three. No, two most days. Three if I've got a revision day or a late shift.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you vape or smoke?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Vape, every day, for about two years. Cigarettes I never really stuck with, just a few in first term at uni, then I packed them in. Mint flavour, which my partner hates, says the flat smells like toothpaste...
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends. Three or four pints, not through the week. Oh, medicines, is that what you're...
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol. Just weekends?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Just weekends.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any regular medicines, or ones you've stopped?

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): They gave me propranolol for the fluttering. Ten milligrams... no, sorry, forty milligrams, once a day. I took it for four days, then I stopped at the beginning of last month, because it wiped me out completely.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else prescribed?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Someone mentioned citalopram for anxiety, but I never took it. I didn't even collect it. I'm not anxious.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Family history of thyroid disease?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): My mum. Overactive thyroid. She had tablets and it settled, years ago. She was round on Sunday actually with this lasagne...
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): You. Weight loss, feeling hot, shaking?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Trousers are looser. I've been skipping meals with the revision, so that might be it. I don't feel particularly hot. My hands only shake when the heart's racing.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Previous heart trouble, asthma, diabetes?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that. Appendix out though, when I was sixteen... no, seventeen. Keyhole, straightforward.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I know of.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Waterworks and bowels, all right?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, all fine. I did have a dodgy stomach after a kebab last month but that's gone, not related, the place on the high street has gone downhill...
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shirt up. Quiet a second while I listen.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): It's freezing in here. The waiting room telly was stuck on some property programme and I nearly...

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no wheeze, heart sounds are normal with no murmur, and the pulse is regular just now. Heart rate ninety-six, blood pressure one hundred and twenty-eight over seventy-eight, oxygen saturations ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): My partner counted about a hundred and twenty at home before a mock exam. Does that mean...
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's not the reading today. I'm arranging an ECG while you're here, and blood tests for your thyroid.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it the thyroid like my mum? Because if I have to take tablets forever I don't know how I'll manage the exams and the cinema job, the manager already...

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can't say yet. It may be ectopic beats stirred up by caffeine and poor sleep, but an arrhythmia or an overactive thyroid both need ruling out. Stop the energy drinks completely. Coffee down to two cups, none after midday.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Two cups? Even on shift days? Without them I just...
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two. And when the fluttering starts, slow breathing, in for four counts, out for six. Practise that twice a day as well.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): My partner already tried to get me doing that and I sort of laughed it off, which was probably...
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do it anyway. If you get chest pain, if you faint, or if the breathlessness comes on suddenly and severely, go to A&E.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): And otherwise?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you in two weeks with the results. Reception will sort the ECG now.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, yeah, all right. I'll try the breathing thing tonight if I remember.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

Light-headedness with the palpitations is described as 'not spinning, just floaty.'
Weight loss is uncertain/qualified: trousers are looser but he attributes it to skipping meals, rather than definite weight loss.
Propranolol was stopped at the beginning of last month because it 'wiped me out completely' (adverse effect/intolerance).
Citalopram was mentioned/prescribed for anxiety but he never took it and did not collect it.

Current heart rate today was specifically stated to be regular and 96 bpm, contrasted with a home rate of about 120 counted by his partner before a mock exam; doctor said that was not today's reading.
